mechanical.root_cause: RENDER-ORDER INVERSION (found by @3D reading the inlined r160): setting renderOrder on a Group becomes groupOrder for its whole subtree, and painterSortStable compares groupOrder BEFORE renderOrder. The count passes were in Groups (groupOrder 1/3/5); the cap quads were direct scene children (groupOrder 0). So the caps drew FIRST, testing NotEqual against a freshly auto-cleared (all-zero) stencil -> every fragment discarded; the count then wrote a buffer nobody read. Fix: group.renderOrder=0, order lives per-child at one groupOrder. This explains every prior measurement (capdebug=2 full magenta = quad placed; capdebug=1 zero = buffer 0 at read time; identical GPU/SwiftShader = deterministic sort bug, not a rasterizer limit; byte-identical before/after = cap drew nothing).

mechanical.note: Spec-less retrofit gate. PASS by MEASURED evidence + @3D's confirmed falsifiable prediction, not pre-look alone (given this session's earlier pre-look bias). The stencil technique is now gateable via the capdebug=1 magenta mode + before/after pixel diff — a legitimate render-path gate that closes the earlier verifiability concern. Decision to stay stencil (vs geometry caps) was correct: the no-op was a code bug (measured identical on GPU and SwiftShader), not renderer fragility, so switching techniques would have carried the same ordering bug into geometry caps undiscovered.
